content.text:
## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}"
on:
  issues:
    types:
      - opened
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: Existing issue to run
permissions: {}
concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    outputs:
      approved: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.approved }}
      issue_number: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Authenticate status callbacks
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
          import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';
          const env = process.env;
          const origin = env.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN.replace(/\/$/, '');
          const url = new URL(env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL);
          url.searchParams.set('audience', origin);
          async function json(url, options) {
            const response = await fetch(url, { ...options, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) });
            if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Callback authentication HTTP ${response.status}`);
            return response.json();
          }
          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 8; attempt++) {
            try {
              const identity = await json(url, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}` } });
              const { token } = await json(`${origin}/api/github/${env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${env.ISSUE_NUMBER}/callback-token`, {
                method: 'POST', headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${identity.value}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
                body: JSON.stringify({ run: env.GITHUB_RUN_ID, attempt: Number(env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT) })
              });
              console.log(`::add-mask::${token}`);

content.text:
We'll create a Vite project with three.js. Need to design a solid, playable 7 Days to Die-like voxel survival game.

Scope plan:
- Voxel world (chunked), procedurally generated terrain: hills, stone, ore, trees, grass/dirt. Destructible blocks (mine) and placeable blocks.
- First-person controls: WASD, mouse look (pointer lock), jump, sprint, crouch? Mining with LMB, placing with RMB.
- Day/night cycle with 7-day horde. HUD: time/day, health, stamina, hunger, thirst, XP/level maybe.
- Zombies: spawn at night / horde on day 7 night; pathfind roughly toward player, damage on touch, can be shot with gun or hit with tool. Blood particles.
- Crafting/inventory: gather wood/stone/iron, craft axe/pickaxe, campfire? Keep a manageable but rich crafting menu.
- Building blocks placement.
- Sound via WebAudio synth (no assets).
- Mobile: touch joystick, look drag, action buttons.
- Menus: title screen with "Survive 7 days" / start, pause, death screen.
- Save/load via localStorage maybe.

Performance: chunk voxel meshing. Need efficient greedy-ish meshing with per-face AO. World 8x8 chunks of 16x64? Use chunks 16x16x64 with heights maybe up to 40. Terrain generation with value noise. Trees, rocks, building ruin maybe.

Rendering: MeshLambert/Standard materials with vertex colors, ambient occlusion baked. Foliage/cross blocks for plants.

This is big. Let's architect files:

- index.html
- src/main.js — bootstrap, game loop
- src/world.js — voxel world, chunks, generation, meshing
- src/player.js — controls, physics, camera
- src/zombies.js — zombie entities
- src/items.js — item/block defs, crafting recipes
- src/hud.js — DOM HUD
- src/ui.js — menus, inventory/crafting screens
- src/audio.js — procedural sfx
- src/mobile.js — touch controls
- src/style.css

Use Vite with three. Should be fine. Let's check three installed via npm install.

Let me think about gameplay depth to make it "complete, playable":

Core loop: spawn on day 1 morning at 08:00. Days last maybe 8 minutes real-time with 2 min day? For playability, day = 240s? Horde at night of day 7. But a session testing should see stuff fast. Make day length 4 min (day 07:00-19:00) then night. And "7 days" is the goal with day counter. Maybe speed: full cycle 6 minutes, night 2 min. Horde night 7 = massive zombies.

Stats: health 100, stamina 100, hunger 100, thirst 100. Hunger/thirst decay slowly. Eating canned food, drinking water. Items found in crates/loot? Add loot containers (wooden crates) in ruins giving food/ammo.

Weapons: stone axe (harvest wood), stone pickaxe (stone/ore), pistol with ammo (craft), bow? Keep melee + pistol. Zombies drop "rotten flesh"? Add bandages from cloth.

Crafting recipes:
- Wood planks? Simplify blocks: dirt, stone, wood log, planks, cobblestone, glass? 
- Tools: Stone Axe (3 wood, 2 stone, 1 cloth?), Stone Pickaxe, Wooden Club, Pistol (needs iron, gunpowder?), ammo.
- Campfire? maybe cooking meat. Keep: campfire placeable that heals? Might be too much.

Simplify to essentials but satisfying: 
Inventory grid with item counts, hotbar 1-6 (axe, pickaxe, pistol, blocks, food, bandage). Drag not needed; click to select.

HUD: bottom hotbar, left stat bars, top center day/time clock, crosshair, damage vignette, horde warning banner, hints.

Mining progression: need pickaxe for stone/iron? Could allow mining stone with any tool slowly. Tool tier affects speed, blocks need correct tool for drop. Simpler: axe speeds wood, pickaxe speeds stone; without tool slow. Iron ore requires pickaxe.

Zombie AI: simple steering toward player, avoid blocks? They can break blocks that block them? 7DTD zombies dig. Implement: if blocked ahead, zombies damage block (slow) and destroy. That's cool. Cap count.

Zombie spawns at night on surface away from player. Day 7 horde spawns waves.

Level/XP: kills give XP, leveling increases max health, gives skill? Keep simple XP and level display.

Save state? LocalStorage checkpoint at dawn. Maybe skip for time but nice. Could add "save on unload" of world modifications + player state. Risk. Add minimal save/load via localStorage of edits map and player stats, day time. Let's consider later.

Meshing: chunk with blocks Uint8Array. Build BufferGeometry with positions, normals, colors (+AO in color). Two meshes per chunk: opaque and transparent (leaves? use opaque leaves with alphaTest texture? No textures, plain colors). Use vertex color variation for texture (noise). Water as transparent-ish block? Add water lakes at sea level, as transparent blue, not solid (can swim? complicated). Maybe skip water to avoid issues; use ponds as decorative "water" with swim slowdown? Skip for now; add sandy areas.

Visual style: low-poly voxel with flat colors + baked AO + fog + sky gradient + sun light shadows? Shadows costly with many chunks. Use directional light without shadow? Voxel colors + AO look decent. Maybe shadows on for zombies/player only? Skip.

Sky: gradient shader background sphere; sun/moon sprites; stars at night. Fog color changes with time.

Post: not needed.

Use instanced meshes? Chunk merged geometry fine.

World size: 12x12 chunks *16 = 192x192, height 48. Edits persisted in Map with key. Fine.

Generation: fBm noise height; biome variation; caves? Maybe simple caves via 3D noise to dig into — adds depth. Iron ore veins underground. Add ruins above ground (small broken houses with crates) to encourage exploration.

Lighting underground: no dynamic light. Player carried torch light (point light) when holding torch? Add point light attached camera to see caves. Nice.

Add simple day/night lighting intensity changes with sky colors.

Mobile: touch joystick left, look drag right, jump + mine + place buttons, hotbar tap.

Screenshot tests: needs to look good. Title screen with dramatic background? Simpler: game starts directly with a "Start" overlay? Capture tool auto-starts by clicking a start button (capture-start.mjs likely looks for button). Let me check capture-start/wip-screenshots to know heuristics.

Good. Start button text should be exactly "Start" or "Play".

Now let's set up project. I'll write substantial code. Let me plan visual design thoroughly since screenshot quality matters.

Title/menu: overlay with dark translucent gradient, game title "7 DAYS TO DIE" style but we should avoid trademark? Building a 7DTD-inspired game is fine; title "7 DAYS TO DIE" requested. Maybe title "SEVEN DAYS" with subtitle "TO DIE". I'll make dramatic red-orange.

On load: show menu over live 3D world (camera panning over terrain) so screenshot looks great. Capture auto-clicks Start then screenshot 1s later — gameplay view. Make sure initial spawn view is scenic: spawn near ruins/trees.

Start: pointer lock requires click gesture; Start button click gives gesture. For headless capture, pointer lock may fail silently—fine.

Gameplay render quality: use three r160+, ACES tone mapping, sRGB, fog, sky shader, sun directional light with shadows? Shadows would help look. Chunk meshes many; a 2048 shadow map covering 100 units around player might be OK. Let's include shadows for blocks (castShadow/receiveShadow on chunk meshes) but frustum size 64, updating with player. Zombies cast shadows too. Performance on SwiftShader might be bad; test. Could make shadows optional based on device. Keep shadows on desktop, off on low-end/mobile.

Textures: procedural canvas textures! Generate 16x16 noise textures per block type, NearestFilter. That will massively improve look vs flat color. Create atlas or per-material textures with vertex colors multiplied. Chunks use single material with texture atlas: build atlas canvas 256x256 with tiles for grass_top, grass_side, dirt, stone, log, leaves, sand, planks, cobble, iron, glass, water, etc. UVs per face. MeshLambertMaterial with map + vertexColors for AO/tint.

Block definitions include per-face tile indices. Atlas generation procedural pixel noise.

Also sky: shader gradient with sun disc. Stars as points. Clouds? Simple flat cloud planes maybe.

Sun/moon directional light + hemisphere light.

Water: lakes at level 14? Could complicate. Instead make "water" blocks as decorative in low basins non-solid, transparent with animated offset? Player swims: if head in water, slower. Let's include simple water: generated in terrain below sea level; block non-collidable, semi-transparent, gives blue tint overlay when camera submerged, swim up. It adds scenic ponds. But meshing transparent per chunk separately. Fine.

Zombie models: low-poly humanoid built from boxes with greenish skin, torn clothes, glowing eyes in dark, arms forward. Animate walk with leg/arm swing. Different variants (walker, runner, brute on day 7). Health bars above? Damage numbers floating.

Player damage: screen red vignette, hurt sound, shake. Death -> death screen with days survived, restart.

Melee: raycast to zombie or block within 3.2m, swing animation with held item mesh in hand (first-person viewmodel): axe/pickaxe/pistol/flashlight/blocks. Viewmodel adds a lot of feel. Build simple box models attached to camera, with idle bob/swing animation. Pistol fires raycast with tracer, muzzle flash light, recoil, ammo count.

Particles: block break instanced cubes with gravity, blood particles, muzzle flash.

Sounds: WebAudio synth: mining thud, break, gunshot noise burst, zombie growl (sawtooth), eat, footsteps, horde horn. Nice.

Crafting: overlay panel E with recipes list; click craft. Inventory items. Hotbar 6 slots mapped to item types:
1 Stone Axe, 2 Pickaxe, 3 Pistol, 4 Wood Block, 5 Stone Block, 6 Food? Actually bandages/food via keys. Hotbar shows selected. Number keys 1-6. Scroll wheel.

Gathering: chop tree logs (gives wood), mine stone (gives stone), iron ore (iron). Loot crates give ammo, food, cloth.

Items inventory: wood, stone, iron, ammo, food, bandage, cloth? Craft:
- Stone Axe: 3 wood + 2 stone
- Stone Pickaxe: 3 wood + 3 stone
- Wooden Club: 4 wood (melee)
- Pistol: 8 iron + 4 wood (start with pistol? better: start with pistol and 12 ammo)
- Ammo x12: 1 iron + 1 wood? gunpowder not available; simplify "ammo" craft 5 iron -> 12 bullets.
- Bandage: 1 cloth (from zombies drop cloth)
- Campfire? skip.
- Wooden Planks block x8: 1 wood -> 4 blocks.
- Cobblestone block x4: 1 stone.

Hotbar editable: selected block types from inventory automatically.

During mining: tier requires: stone/iron needs pickaxe? To be forgiving: stone can be mined by hand slowly, iron requires pickaxe. Show tooltip.

Day/night: start Day 1 at 09:00; time scale: 1 real sec = 1 game min? 1 day = 24 min too long. Use 1 real sec = 2.4 game min => 10 min day. For a game session, fine. Horde night day 7 arrives ~60 min. Too long for demo but they can sleep? Add "Sleep in bed"? Hmm. Provide dev-ish time acceleration? User can't be expected to play 7 days. It's a game; progression is the point. But for showcasing, add options: "Skip to Night" key? Maybe add a "rest" feature: stand at bed/shelter to pass time? Alternatively make days ~3 minutes: 1 sec = 8 game min => 24*60/8 = 180s per day. 7 days = 21 minutes. That's reasonable. Night 8 min? Day 07:00-19:00 12h = 90s, night 90s. Hordes manageable. I'll use 180s/day, with day phase 07:00-19:30.

Horde night: waves scale with day; on night 7 big horde announces "THE HORDE IS COMING". Zombies spawn continuously for the night. Survive till dawn. Win screen if survive day 7 horde: "You survived 7 days". Actually game continues; show victory overlay and allow continue.

But also we want the world at night to look good. Night horde is cool with muzzle flashes.

Zombie block breaking: implement when target path blocked and within 1.5m of player... they should attack player when close. For pathing through walls: if zombie stuck for a while and near player, damage the block in front, break after N hits. Include.

Chunk collision: raycast AABB per voxel; player physics: AABB vs blocks, step up? Player capsule as AABB 0.6x1.8. Movement with gravity, jump. Ground detection.

Chunk mesh rebuild on edit; neighbor updates for border faces (we have greedy? simple per-face culling with neighbor chunk lookup).

Chunk generation lazily around player? For simplicity generate whole world upfront async in chunks over frames with progress. World 160x160 with height 64 = 1.6M blocks okay. 10x10 chunks = 100 chunks. Meshing 100 chunks at start might take a few seconds. Do it with loading screen progress. Then screenshot after start click gives 1s... loading could be done during menu? Generate world during menu (before Start) so screenshot immediate. Good: show loading only if slow but start button disabled? Capture clicks Start within 3s; if loading blocks... We'll generate synchronously in menu with async chunked generation showing progress, enable Start when done. But capture auto-clicks after load event + 1s; if button not present/disabled at that time it gives "not-found". Risk. So generate the world quickly (<1s) enough. Use 8x8 chunks of 16 -> 128 area, height 56. 8*16=128 wide. ~917k voxels; generation fine. Meshing 64 chunks, each 16x16x56 faces — maybe 200-400ms total. OK.

Alternatively generate full world synchronously at startup. Let's do sync generation and meshing in a loop with progress bar + yielding, but capture issue. Better: generate synchronously before showing menu. Loading screen briefly (~1-2s), then menu. page load happens before? page.goto waits load which includes module execution (our sync work blocks load event). Then Start button visible. Fine.

Menu background: world render with slow camera orbit. Good screenshot.

export function blockDef(id) { return BLOCKS[id] || BLOCKS[B.AIR] }
export function isSolid(id) { return blockDef(id).solid === true }
export function isOpaque(id) {
  const d = blockDef(id)
  return d.solid && !d.transparent
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable voxel survival game inspired by 7 Days to Die, with exploration, mining/building, combat, survival stats, crafting, zombies, and a day/night horde system.

## Requirements
- Must be a complete playable browser game.
- No clarifying questions; reasonable assumptions allowed.
- Desktop and mobile interaction should both be supported.

## Decisions
- Used Three.js for rendering and Vite as the build system.
- Implemented an original voxel survival experience rather than copyrighted assets or exact game replication.
- Assumed a 160×160 procedural world with 16-block chunks and a 200-second day length.

## Work State
### Completed
- Procedural voxel world generation, terrain, roads, water, caves, trees, cabins, POIs, and campfires.
- Block atlas and block types with mining, placing, transparency, textures, and saves.
- First-person player movement, jumping, stamina, hunger, thirst, health, XP, and death.
- Stone axe/pickaxe, pistol, ammo, consumables, inventory, hotbar, crafting, and block placement.
- Zombie walkers, runners, and brutes with horde spawning and blood/loot effects.
- Dynamic sky, clouds, sun/moon, lighting, fog, weather-like atmosphere, audio, and particle FX.
- Main menu, HUD, pause screen, inventory, crafting, death/victory screens, and save/load.
- Mobile touch controls and first-person held-item models.
- Vite build setup and local preview server setup.
- Basic visual and runtime checks using browser screenshots and game state inspection.

### Active
- Polishing visuals and validating interactions; work is substantially implemented but may need final browser verification.

### Blocked
- None noted.

## Next Move
1. Run a final `npx vite build --base ./` and serve the resulting game.
2. Verify menu-to-game flow, mining, placing, inventory, crafting, zombie combat, pause, save/load, and death.
3. Check desktop and mobile layouts for HUD overlap and held-item rendering.
4. Capture and inspect a final small JPEG screenshot at 1280×800 or smaller.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: Main game loop, state, input, saves, combat, and interactions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: World generation, chunk meshing, blocks, raycasts, buildings, and POIs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: Player movement, survival stats, camera, and held models.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/zombies.js`: Zombie AI, spawning, horde behavior, and combat.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: HUD, inventory, crafting, menus, notifications, and end screens.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/sky.js`: Day/night cycle, sky, clouds, sun/moon, and lighting.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/textures.js`: Procedural texture atlas and UV generation.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/blocks.js`: Block definitions and properties.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/items.js`: Items, recipes, inventory icons, and crafting rules.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/fx.js`: Particle effects, tracers, and damage numbers.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: Procedural sound effects and ambient audio.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/mobile.js`: Touch movement and action controls.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/style.css`: Complete game styling and responsive layouts.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Application markup and UI structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: Vite build scripts and dependencies.

## Important Context
- Browser debug state is exposed as `window.__game`.
- `SAVE_KEY` is `seven-days-to-die-save-v1`.
- Default world dimensions are `WORLD_SIZE = 160`, `HEIGHT = 64`, and `SEA_LEVEL = 23`.
- Day length is 200 seconds.
- Desktop controls include WASD, mouse look, E inventory, I inventory, Space jump, left/right mouse actions, and number hotbar keys.
- Mobile controls are created by `setupMobile(game, input)` and require a touch-capable device or touch emulation.
- The game state is largely implemented but should receive a final integrated interaction pass after reload/build.
